Stress.title: Slow breathing
Stress.subtitle: Breathe in for 4, out for 6
steps: Sit comfortably and let your shoulders drop.
Breathe in gently through your nose for 4 seconds.
Breathe out slowly for 6 seconds.
Keep it soft. No need to hold your breath.

Stress.title: Tense and release
Stress.subtitle: Let go of tension, one area at a time
steps: Make fists for 5 seconds, then let go for 10.
Lift your shoulders to your ears for 5 seconds, then drop them.
Scrunch your face for 5 seconds, then relax it.
Notice the difference between tense and relaxed.

Stress.title: Calm music break
Stress.subtitle: Five minutes of music you find soothing
steps: Pick a calm track you like.
Close your eyes or look somewhere soft.
Just listen until the timer ends.

Stress.title: Physiological sigh
Stress.subtitle: Double inhale, long slow exhale
steps: Breathe in through your nose.
Take a second, short sip of air on top.
Breathe out slowly and fully through your mouth.
Repeat at a comfortable pace.

Stress.title: Talk to yourself like a friend
Stress.subtitle: Use your own name to get some distance
steps: Think about what's stressing you.
Write two sentences about it using your name instead of 'I', e.g. 'Sam is worried because…'.
Add one sentence of advice you'd give a friend in Sam's place.

Stress.title: Kind words to yourself
Stress.subtitle: A short self-compassion pause
steps: Notice: 'This is a hard moment.'
Remember: 'Lots of people feel this way.'
Offer yourself one kind sentence, the way you would to a friend.

Stress.title: Get it out of your head
Stress.subtitle: List what's on your plate and the very next step
steps: List the things on your mind.
For one of them, write the very next small step and when you'll do it.
Let the list hold the rest for now.

Stress.title: Picture a calm place
Stress.subtitle: A short guided visualisation
steps: Close your eyes and picture a place where you feel at ease.
Notice what you can see, hear and feel there.
Stay with it for a few slow breaths.

Stress.title: Something funny
Stress.subtitle: A few minutes of comedy you enjoy
steps: Watch or listen to something that usually makes you laugh.
Come back and tap done when you're finished.

Stress.title: Ten-minute walk
Stress.subtitle: A brisk walk at your own pace
steps: Head outside or walk around indoors.
Pick a pace that feels brisk but comfortable.
Tap done when you're back.

Anxiety.title: Slow breathing
Anxiety.subtitle: Breathe in for 4, out for 6
steps: Sit comfortably and let your shoulders drop.
Breathe in gently through your nose for 4 seconds.
Breathe out slowly for 6 seconds.
Keep it soft. No need to hold your breath.

Anxiety.title: Tense and release
Anxiety.subtitle: Let go of tension, one area at a time
steps: Make fists for 5 seconds, then let go for 10.
Lift your shoulders to your ears for 5 seconds, then drop them.
Scrunch your face for 5 seconds, then relax it.
Notice the difference between tense and relaxed.

Anxiety.title: Colour a mandala
Anxiety.subtitle: Fill in a pattern, no skill needed
steps: Pick any colours you like.
Fill in the shapes at your own pace.
There's no right or wrong way.

Anxiety.title: Park the worry
Anxiety.subtitle: Write it down and set a time to think about it later
steps: Write the worry in one line.
Pick a 15-minute 'worry time' later today.
Until then, when it comes back, remind yourself it's parked.

Anxiety.title: Kind words to yourself
Anxiety.subtitle: A short self-compassion pause
steps: Notice: 'This is a hard moment.'
Remember: 'Lots of people feel this way.'
Offer yourself one kind sentence, the way you would to a friend.

Anxiety.title: Talk to yourself like a friend
Anxiety.subtitle: Use your own name to get some distance
steps: Think about what's worrying you.
Write two sentences about it using your name instead of 'I'.
Add one sentence of advice you'd give a friend in your place.

Anxiety.title: Next small step
Anxiety.subtitle: Turn one worry into a plan
steps: Write what you're worried might happen.
Write one small thing you can do about it, and when.
If there's nothing to do, note that too and let it rest.

Anxiety.title: Calm music break
Anxiety.subtitle: Five minutes of music you find soothing
steps: Pick a calm track you like.
Close your eyes or look somewhere soft.
Just listen until the timer ends.

Anxiety.title: Get moving
Anxiety.subtitle: 20 minutes of exercise you enjoy, at a comfortable pace
steps: Pick something you enjoy: a brisk walk, cycling, a home workout.
Keep the pace comfortable; you should still be able to talk.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
Tap done when you're back.

Mental Fatigue.title: Proper micro-break
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: Step away from the screen for a few minutes
steps: Look away from your screen.
Stretch, get a drink or look out of a window.
Come back when the timer ends.

Mental Fatigue.title: Stand up and move
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: A few minutes of light movement
steps: Stand up and roll your shoulders.
Walk around the room or march on the spot.
Reach up high, then shake out your arms.

Mental Fatigue.title: Ten-minute walk
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: A brisk walk for a lift in energy
steps: Head outside if you can.
Walk briskly but comfortably.
Tap done when you're back.

Mental Fatigue.title: Short power nap
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: Ten minutes, set an alarm
steps: Find somewhere you can lie down or rest your head.
Set an alarm for 10 minutes.
Not in the late afternoon or evening if it affects your sleep.

Mental Fatigue.title: Green view
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: Sit somewhere green, or look at trees through a window
steps: Find a green spot or a window with a view of trees or plants.
Let your eyes rest on it without your phone.
Tap done when you're ready.

Mental Fatigue.title: Get some daylight
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: Spend a few minutes in bright daylight
steps: Step outside or sit by a bright window during the day.
Stay for a few minutes.
Tap done when you're back.

Mental Fatigue.title: Take the stairs
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: Ten minutes of easy stair walking
steps: Walk up and down a flight of stairs at a gentle pace.
Hold the rail and stop if you feel unwell.
Tap done when you're finished.

Mental Fatigue.title: Dance it out
Mental Fatigue.subtitle: One upbeat song, move however you like
steps: Pick a song you like.
Move however feels good.
No one's watching.

Calm Flow.title: Savour this moment
Calm Flow.subtitle: Notice what feels good right now
steps: Notice one thing you can see, hear or feel that you're enjoying.
Stay with it for a few breaths.
Write a word or two about it if you like.

Calm Flow.title: Green view
Calm Flow.subtitle: Sit somewhere green for a few minutes
steps: Find a green spot or a window with a view of trees or plants.
Let your eyes rest on it without your phone.
Tap done when you're ready.

Calm Flow.title: Kindness meditation
Calm Flow.subtitle: Send warm wishes to yourself and others
steps: Silently wish yourself: 'May I be well.'
Picture someone you care about and wish them the same.
Extend it to someone you barely know.

Calm Flow.title: Three good photos
Calm Flow.subtitle: Photograph three things you like around you
steps: Look around for things that make you smile.
Take three photos.
Look back at them later today.

Calm Flow.title: Three good things
Calm Flow.subtitle: Note what's going well
steps: Write three things that went well or you're glad about.
For one of them, add why it happened.

Calm Flow.title: Colour a mandala
Calm Flow.subtitle: Keep the calm going with colour
steps: Pick colours you like.
Fill in the shapes at your own pace.

Calm Flow.title: Awe walk
Calm Flow.subtitle: A walk looking for things that amaze you
steps: Go for a short walk somewhere new or familiar.
Look for things that feel vast or surprising: sky, trees, buildings, details.
Tap done when you're back.

Calm Flow.title: Slow breathing
Calm Flow.subtitle: Stay in the calm
steps: Breathe in for 4 seconds.
Breathe out for 6 seconds.
Enjoy the stillness.

Radiant Joy.title: Savour this moment
Radiant Joy.subtitle: Stay with the good feeling a bit longer
steps: Notice what you're enjoying right now.
Replay the best part in your mind.
Write a word or two about it if you like.

Radiant Joy.title: Small kind act
Radiant Joy.subtitle: Do one small thing for someone else
steps: Pick one small kind thing: a compliment, a thank-you, a helping hand.
Do it today.
Tap done when you have.

Radiant Joy.title: Share the good news
Radiant Joy.subtitle: Tell someone what went well
steps: Think of someone who'd be happy for you.
Send a message or call to tell them what went well.

Radiant Joy.title: Best possible future
Radiant Joy.subtitle: Write about life going really well
steps: Imagine a future where things have gone as well as they could.
Write about what it looks like.
Keep it realistic and specific.

Radiant Joy.title: Thank-you note
Radiant Joy.subtitle: Write to someone who helped you
steps: Think of someone you never properly thanked.
Write them a short note about what they did and why it mattered.
Send it if you'd like to.

Radiant Joy.title: Try something new
Radiant Joy.subtitle: Use the good mood to explore
steps: Pick something small you've wanted to try: a new route, recipe or idea.
Give it a go for ten minutes.

Radiant Joy.title: Dance it out
Radiant Joy.subtitle: One upbeat song, move however you like
steps: Pick a song you love.
Move however feels good.

Radiant Joy.title: Make something
Radiant Joy.subtitle: Draw, write or build anything for fun
steps: Make anything you like: a doodle, a short poem, a little design.
Play, don't judge.
